project: Predict New York City Airbnb Prices
business_summary: On 9,164 held-out typical-market listings, R-squared is 0.4654: the model explains about 46.5% of variation in listed nightly prices. This is not classification accuracy. MAE is $38.60 per night, meaning that the average prediction misses the listed price by that amount in either direction. RMSE is $53.06, which puts extra weight on larger misses. The mean-price baseline has MAE $58.21, so the model reduces average absolute error by 33.7% against that baseline. These results concern prices at or below $355.70 and minimum stays at or below 30 nights. On all 9,777 held-out positive-price listings, including excluded luxury and long-stay rows, MAE is $63.16 and R-squared is 0.0798. Use the estimate as an initial benchmark, with human review and current comparable listings before choosing a real asking price.
price_band_interpretation: The model performs better on inexpensive listings in absolute dollar terms. MAE is $25.86 for prices up to $66, compared with $63.69 for prices above $160. The expensive band has a mean actual-minus-predicted residual of $59.19. A positive residual indicates underestimation. Ordinary least squares pulls fitted values toward the central price pattern; larger prices can have larger dollar errors. Unobserved size, amenities, quality and nonlinear location effects are plausible additional explanations, rather than causes established by this dataset. Relative errors tell a different part of the story: MAPE is 58.5% for inexpensive listings and 25.6% for expensive listings. Therefore, lower dollar error does not automatically mean better percentage accuracy.
